critique: The broad absorbing-face theorem identifies active component sublaws, unnormalized type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate ATT; full type shares and full conditional type effects are proved only on the no-date-1-absorption subface. The initial-absorber construction establishes class-level nonidentification outside that subface, but it is not a pointwise characterization of every law with initial absorption, so “sharp frontier” must retain that class-level meaning. The inference result establishes efficiency only for the chosen off-model extension in the saturated finite-multinomial model, while restricted-Markov efficiency remains explicitly open. Known J, fixed anchors, simple spectra, and nonsingularity of the full anchor star materially narrow the result, but the constructive boundary identification theorem itself is non-obvious and complete enough for the field tier.
